Subject: Follow-up: long-window compatibility & truncation observations

Evan / Sara — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of notes from call:
- Primary use case: visit history summarization across 12–24 months of encounters (avg ~8k tokens per patient document; some up to ~60k).
- Key constraints: low latency for UI summaries (<1.2s token latency), strict PII handling, and predictable per-PAAS cost.
- Main concern you raised: how Redwood handles documents that exceed a model's context window (truncation behavior / fidelity of summaries).

Preliminary recommendations (internal + product):
- Short-term pilot: run our "long-window summarization" recipe with a 64k context model variant + prefix-KV caching.
- Benchmarks we'll run: truncation-failure rate, hallucination incidence on boundary spans, summary fidelity vs. oracle (ROUGE/L-based + human spot checks).

What we need from ChartWell to scope the pilot:
1) 3 representative patient threads (de-identified) that exercise long history and mid-record edits (example file formats: .txt or exported EHR note JSON).
2) a prioritized prompt set (we created a starter set and attached it — chartwell_prompt_set_v1.txt).
3) baseline SLA and latency expectations for the UI flow.

Next steps / asks (proposed timeline):
- You share the three sample de-id files by Tue 04/06.
- Redwood runs an initial run on our 64k-quant model profile and returns a benchmark CSV + a short report by Mon 04/12.
- If the initial run looks good, we propose a 6-week pilot with a canary rollout in production.

Attachments: chartwell_prompt_set_v1.txt (starter prompts), chartwell_requirements_v2.pdf (notes I took during call).

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes

rafael@redwood.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Hi Evan — Neha from Redwood research/solutions here. Short answers and the technical appendix we'll run for your samples: 

Answers to Rafael/Evan's Qs:
- Cost delta (ballpark): our 64k-quant profile typically runs ~2.8–3.5x the per-token runtime cost of a 16k non-quant baseline depending on batch efficiency; caching can reduce effective cost for repeated prefixes by ~30–50%.
- Prefix-KV caching: no schema changes required on ChartWell's side. It's a serving-side optimization: we persist key/value cache for long prefixes between calls to avoid re-encoding earlier tokens. We'll provide an SDK flag and config; only need you to surface stable document IDs in the request metadata so cache keys are consistent.
- Fidelity rubric (short):
  1) Completeness (0–3): percent clinical events captured vs. oracle notes.
  2) Temporal accuracy (0–2): event order preserved.
  3) Hallucination severity (0–3): false-positive clinical claims.
  4) Conciseness (0–2): extraneous content penalty.
  5) Redaction safety check (pass/fail): PHI removal verified.

Planned benchmark outputs (we'll share CSV):
- truncation_failure_rate (% of summaries that drop earliest events)
- rouge_l_oracle (automated proxy)
- human_fidelity_score (rubric average)
- median_latency_ms (token-serving path)

Known regression risks we will monitor:
- Boundary hallucinations when prompts slice across event transitions.
- Summary drift for very long timelines (>40k tokens) where compression heuristics trade fidelity for brevity.
- Tokenization mismatches for non-standard characters in older notes (we'll preprocess but flag).

Attached for your review: a starter prompt set (we've iterated on the attachment Rafael included) and the benchmark schema. We'll also produce a short runbook for redaction and sample de-id guidance.

If you want, we can run an A/B between two model profiles (64k-quant vs 32k-peak with aggressive chunk stitching) as part of the initial run to surface cost/quality trade-offs. That will add ~2 business days to the first delivery.

-Neha
